core_concepts: A man hands me the winner’s check
With the check still folded in my jeans pocket, I stand two days later in my father’s living room and employ a bit of remedial psychology
Goodthen you won’t mind if I buy a car
I know just the kind I want
At the car dealership my father goes back and forth with the salesman, and the negotiation quickly turns contentious
The salesman and my father eventually agree on a price
Small fee for the paperwork, the salesman says
The salesman doesn’t care for my father’s tone
mechanisms_or_explanations: I win my first tournament as a pro, in Itaparica, Brazil, all the more impressive because I do it before a crowd of initially hostile Brazilians
Pops, I say, how much do you think I’m going to make next year?
Goodthen you won’t mind if I buy a car
I wonder what I could do in tennis if I could access that rage and aim it across the net
Mom, I ask, how do you take it?

Few things give Lenny more pleasure than abusing me and hurling obscenities at me in the process
I feel as if I’m starting to get tennis
I cringe when fans start dressing like mebut I also dig it
If you don’t want those, Mac, I’ve got dibs
If I can’t understand my motivations and demons, how can I hope to explain them to journalists on deadline?
To make matters worse, journalists write down exactly what I say, while I’m saying it, word for word, as if this represented the literal truth
critical_qualifiers: I no longer live full-time at the Bolletieri Academy, so once again I live under my father’s roof, and thus under his control

My knowledge of the game is improving, but my body is breaking down

The way they watch me and ask for my autograph, the way they scream as I enter an arena, makes me uncomfortable, but also satisfies something deep inside me, some hidden craving I didn’t know was there
They call me a rebel, but I have no interest in being a rebel, I’m only conducting an everyday, run-of-the-mill teenage rebellion
But I’m doing it on a grander stage
important_examples: I consider myself a Christian, but J.P.’s church is the first one where I’ve felt truly close to God
key_entities_or_numbers: I’m only seventeen, not ready to live on my own, barely ready to stand alone on a tennis court, and yet I was just in Rio, holding a girl in a thong with one hand and a $90,000 check with the other
Pops, the car costs $37,000, and you’re flipping out about a $50 fee?
In December 1987 the desert turns unseasonably cold
I win the first tournament of 1988, in Memphis, and the ball sounds alive as it leaves my racket
Dressing like me in 1988 means wearing denim shorts
AT INDIAN WELLS, in February 1988, I blaze my way to the semis, where I meet Boris Becker, from West Germany, the most famous tennis player in the world
After three rounds of the Italian Open, in May 1988, I’m no longer Andre Agassi
